title: Degenerate high-order hybrid bound states in the continuum beyond diffraction limit
authors: Ji Tong Wang, Nicolae C. Panoiu
abstract: We demonstrate the existence of at-$Γ$ degenerate hybrid bound-states in the continuum (BICs) with high-order topological charges and quadratic band degeneracy in periodic photonic structures with $C_{6v}$ symmetry above the diffraction limit. The degenerate BICs are realized by combining symmetry protection, which suppresses radiation into zeroth-order diffraction channel, with quadratic band degeneracy and parameter tuning to eliminate radiation into first-order diffraction channels. An effective Hamiltonian is used to investigate the band structure around the degeneracy point, and the topological dynamics in all diffraction channels are characterized. This work reveals a novel mechanism for realizing degenerate BICs above the diffraction limit, opening up opportunities for new physics and applications.
summary: This paper theoretically demonstrates how to create highly confined, degenerate bound states in the continuum (h-BICs) within photonic crystal structures beyond their normal diffraction limits. By leveraging $C_{6v}$ symmetry and tuning structural parameters, the authors suppress radiation into multiple diffraction channels simultaneously. This opens pathways for designing novel optical devices with enhanced light-matter interaction governed by topological physics.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate the existence of degenerate hybrid bound states in the continuum (h-BICs) possessing high-order topological charges, specifically operating beyond the standard diffraction limit.
main_result: A novel mechanism is proposed and shown to realize at-Gamma degenerate h-BICs by combining symmetry protection for the zeroth order and parameter tuning to eliminate radiation into first-order channels. The frequency splitting near degeneracy scales quadratically and isotropically.
method: The study employs an effective Hamiltonian approach, derived from analyzing band structures in photonic crystals, combined with topological charge calculations via winding numbers.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Photonic Crystal (PhC) slab exhibiting $C_{6v}$ symmetry. The analysis uses an effective Hamiltonian $	ilde{H}_{	ext{eff}}$ whose eigenvalues govern the frequency and leakage rate dispersion ($\omega \pm i\gamma$) around the degeneracy point.
key_observables: Q-factor ($Q$), topological charges (V points), band structure, and far-field polarization maps.
important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the regime beyond the diffraction limit, characterized by geometric parameters $	ilde{r}$ and $	ilde{d}$, and momentum $|\mathbf{k}_\parallel|$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption involves using an effective Hamiltonian model to approximate the band structure near the degeneracy point, which shows good agreement for small in-plane wavevectors ($|\mathbf{k}_\parallel| < 0.02$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of h-BIC formation mechanisms, the degenerate band structure and Q-factor distribution at $\Gamma$, and the dependence of the Q-factor on structural parameters ($	ilde{r}, 	ilde{d}$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical system (PhC slab) and the theoretical framework using an effective Hamiltonian. It then details the mechanism for achieving degeneracy by suppressing radiation in multiple diffraction channels, followed by numerical validation of the scaling laws and topological features.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it deals with engineered photonic band gaps (BICs) that exhibit extreme confinement and topological properties. The concept of controlling leakage rates via symmetry protection is a key tool in designing high-quality optical cavities for quantum applications.
